subject: DPA: deployment-specific data flow & subprocessor questions
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire.d@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, acme-legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sending the DPA earlier this morning. A couple of quick clarifying questions from legal and procurement before we proceed to signatures:

1) We noticed the DPA references subprocessors with a 30-day notification window. For our on-prem/private deployments we usually require either a 14-day notice or the ability to opt-out of a new subprocessor for regulated data. Is Redwood open to a shorter notification period for Private/VPC?

2) For Dedicated (reserved capacity) deployments, can you confirm whether telemetry and aggregate usage metrics are retained by Redwood and whether they could contain identifiers that would cause us to classify that data as PHI under our policies?

3) Cross-border transfer: we need to make sure the DPA covers transfer mechanisms for EU-origin data. We previously told legal that Dedicated customers may still traverse US-based control plane systems. Where does Redwood stand on SCCs/standard contractual clauses for hosted vs private deployments?

We want to keep momentum; procurement is ready to route for signature once legal signs off on these items.

Appreciate your help—Claire

--
Claire Donovan
Head of Legal Operations, Acme Health
claire.d@acmehealth.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Donovan <claire.d@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, acme-legal@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing answers and next steps below to make this trackable.

1) Subprocessor notice window (Private/VPC/on-prem): We can shorten the notification window for Private deployments to 14 days. For on-prem air-gapped installs we can provide advance notice and a signed addendum if desired; opt-out is tricky once a subprocessor is operational, but we can add a clause allowing you to object in writing within 14 days which triggers a mitigation discussion (e.g., contractual restriction, technical isolation).

2) Telemetry in Dedicated: By default, Dedicated customers get aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) associated with a customer id. We do not log prompt text or model outputs in telemetry. If Acme requires, we can provide a telemetry minimization profile (redact token-level identifiers and TTL-delete aggregated logs) as an addendum. Let me know whether you want that default changed for your commitment.

3) Cross-border transfers: For hosted & Dedicated (control plane in US) we use SCCs + EU-US Transfer Impact Assessments where relevant and offer additional contractual safeguards. For Private (VPC/On-prem) you control the compute region and any model serving stays within your VPC; our control-plane metadata may still cross borders for billing/ops. We propose SCCs + a narrow transfer clause limited to metadata for Private customers that want it.

Attachments: I am attaching our current subprocessor roster and a short redline summary that implements the 14-day notice and telemetry minimization option as discussed.

Proposed next step: If Acme legal is comfortable, we can apply the redline and send a DocuSign envelope for your countersignature tomorrow. Marcus / Karthik — please see inline suggested language below and confirm.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Thanks Naomi — a few practical redlines I recommend we include in the DPA we send to Acme:

- Section (Subprocessors): Change "30 days' notice" to "14 days' notice for Private/VPC and on-prem deployments; 30 days' notice for Hosted/Dedicated". Add: "Customer may object in writing within 14 days; if parties cannot agree, Customer may suspend new data flows to the affected subprocessor until a resolution is reached."

- Section (Telemetry): Add a checkbox-style addendum called "Telemetry Minimization" that removes token-level payloads from our logs, reduces retention to 30 days, and provides an option for Strawman audit logs (sampling on request). Default remains aggregated customer id metrics for Dedicated unless Acme elects minimization.

- Section (Transfers): Insert a narrow SCCs commitment for control-plane metadata and offer the option to include a Transfer Addendum for Dedicated customers that process EU data through US control-plane. For Private/VPC deployments hosted entirely in EU, mark control-plane transfers as restricted to operational needs only.

- Execution: We'll send via DocuSign. Recommend we prepare two DocuSign envelopes: one for the DPA redline + subprocessor list, and a separate envelope for the Subprocessor Addendum (so they can accept one without touching the larger master agreement).

If Acme agrees, I'll prepare the envelopes and Naomi / legal can review before sending.

On a compliance note: please confirm whether Acme needs SOC 2 Type II evidence attestation attached to the envelope (we can include a SOC 2 link).

-Marcus

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Adding a technical note for the thread so legal has clarity on what to expect operationally: 

- Private/VPC (customer-managed): All model serving and KV/cache remain inside the VPC and on the customer's subnets. Our installer includes explicit configuration to block outbound egress except to the control-plane endpoints needed for billing/health pings; those pings can be disabled if Acme elects fully air-gapped install.

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed hardware): Data plane stays in the region you pick; control-plane metadata for autoscaling/health may transit to our operations region. We can provide a hardened telemetry profile and an SLA that specifies what metadata is captured and for how long.

- Subprocessor isolation: For Private installs we can lock subprocessor integrations behind customer-controlled gateways (i.e., we don't enable third-party logging agents by default).

Happy to draft a short technical appendix that maps the DPA clauses to concrete controls (endpoints, retention windows, sample audit logs).

-Karthik
